'''Hoti''' is an extinct [[Austronesian languages|Austronesian]] language of [[Seram]], [[Indonesia]], once spoken by the Hoti People. It was spoken by 10 elderly people in 1987, but was likely extinct by 2007.<ref>{{Cite book |url=https://www.academia.edu/5412843/Encyclopeia_of_the_Worlds_Endangered_Languages |title=Encyclopedia of the world's endangered languages |date=2007 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-0-415-56331-4 |editor-last=Moseley |editor-first=Christopher |edition=1st |location=London}}</ref> It is said to have been replaced by [[Geser language|Geser]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Collins |first=James T. |date=1982 |title=Linguistic Research in Maluku: A Report of Recent Field Work |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/3623155 |journal=Oceanic Linguistics |volume=21 |issue=1/2 |pages=73–146 |doi=10.2307/3623155 |issn=0029-8115|url-access=subscription }}</ref>
